articleText:
[Hacker News — github.com]
The open decision compiler Compile your intent once with an LLM. Then decide on every record forever — classification, scoring, routing — as type-safe JSON with probabilities and confidence, on your own hardware, at zero marginal cost .

Agents at compile time. Never at runtime. pip install strot-ai import strot result = strot . run ( tickets , query = "Triage incoming support tickets into the correct workflow." , action_registry = { "billing_dispute" : "Refunds, invoice corrections, double charges" , "technical_defect" : "Crashes, bugs, broken behavior" , }, llm = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-8" , # used once, on first compile only ) for o in result . outcomes : print ( o [ "action" ], round ( o [ "confidence" ], 2 )) # billing_dispute 0.97 # technical_defect 0.94 The LLM runs once , at compile time. Production is a frozen, self-contained Python artifact: a small local decision model arbitrates every record, nothing is generated, every output is bounded, and low-confidence records abstain instead of guessing.

STROT = Agentic Schema Intent + Compiler & State + Code + Execution + NLU ⟹ JSON Decisions (classification · scoring · routing · typed answers) How it works COMPILE (once per intent + schema) intent + sample ─▶ synthesize ─▶ golden gate ─▶ teacher labels ─▶ calibrate (labels, (your known (annotate (fit the projection, answers must a sample, confidence handlers) pass) once) threshold) │ ▼ frozen artifact (.py) RUNTIME (every record, forever) record ─▶ projection ─▶ decision model ─▶ confidence gate ─▶ typed JSON (compiled) (144M, CPU, (decide or decision ~60 ms) abstain) Two surfaces run() — route each record to an action and execute the compiled handler.

decide() — answer typed questions (choice / score / boolean) per record:

result = strot . decide ( records , questions = { "is_bug_report" : { "type" : "boolean" , "instructions" : "mentions crashes/errors?" }, "customer_sentiment" :{ "type" : "score" , "min" : 1 , "max" : 5 , "instructions" : "1 angry, 5 happy" }, "routing_bucket" : { "type" : "choice" , "options" : [ "billing" , "engineering" , "spam" ]}, }) # → {"booleans": {...}, "scores": {...}, "choices": {...}} with probabilities + confidence Measured Real model (SupersonicLabs/Julia-1, 144M, CPU), real datasets, clean Docker containers:

Reproduce everything: benchmarks/ — with the losses published too.

Compile once, decide forever — content-addressed artifact cache; schema drift triggers exactly one recompile. Golden-record promotion — artifacts must pass your known answers before they serve. Fitted guarantees — temperature scaling + split conformal prediction, baked in: dispatched decisions are wrong ≤ α of all records (marginal); the rest abstain. Measured, not guessed — the compiler scores labelings, and can train a distilled head, keeping only what beats the baseline on held-out data. 0% structural hallucination — output is selection + computation over your registry; nothing is generated at runtime. Model-independent — the decision model is a slot ( nlu= ): local Julia-1 by default, hosted APIs, or any drop-in specialist. Install pip install strot-ai # core: pure stdlib pip install strot-ai[local] # + the local decision model (torch/transformers) pip install strot-ai[hosted] # + openai, for a hosted decision runtime pip install strot-ai[anthropic] # + anthropic, for the synthesizer Bake the local model into your image for offline production:

RUN pip install strot-ai[local] \ && python -c "import strot; strot.prefetch_nlu(local_dir='/opt/julia-1', install=True)" ENV STROT_NLU_CHECKPOINT=/opt/julia-1 (Never pip install julia — unrelated package.)

DEVELOPERS.md — architecture, compile lifecycle, calibration semantics and caveats, deployment, model swapping, full API reference.

MIT. Default decision model: Apache-2.0 ( SupersonicLabs/Julia-1 ). Implements ideas from STROT (arXiv:2505.01636).

[Hacker News] I love the concept, but tried reading the README on the got, but I am still unclear about precisely what it does or how it does it. Some more detail would be welcome.
[Hacker News] >On tweet hate-speech it hits the model's ceiling This sounds like a sus endeavor to redline your LLM with, could you elaborate ?
[Hacker News] Yes, even the comment you replied to is very noticeably claude authored.

[Hacker News] > If a ghost is close (nearest_ghost_distance small, " "within 2 steps), choose flee_ghost. Otherwise choose " "chase_dot to eat the nearest dot." Dude, this is AI psychosis. Just ask the LLM to write you a program (“compile”) and then you can run it locally forever
